title: Existing bounded dévissage of a class-relative heart upper bound
statement: Let C,D be abelian categories with unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let Φ:D(C)→D(D) be triangulated and commute with integer shifts [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Let P be a replete class of C containing zero. Suppose d∈ℤ and Φ(M[0]) lies in degrees at most d for every M∈P. For any bounded K with all H^i(K)∈P, if K is at most n, then Φ(K) is at most n+d. Standard good truncations have the meaning of [def-kun-truncations].

source.place: Bounded below paragraph restricted to finite cohomological intervals; existing source bounded dévissage proof

proof.text: For a one-degree complex K=H^n(K)[-n], commute Φ through the shift and use the heart upper bound. Repleteness transports membership through the canonical cohomology isomorphism. For general bounded K choose a lower bound a and induct on max(0,n-a). The triangle τ<n K→K→τ≥n K has its first term one degree shorter and its third term in degree n. Truncation preserves P-cohomology because surviving cohomology is unchanged and discarded cohomology is zero. Apply Φ; extension closure of D^{≤n+d} finishes the induction. A zero complex or an empty interval gives the zero case.
